I am trying to study general tilt GBs in FCC Ni, with tilt axis <110>. Please build and relax an FCC Ni {110} || {111} grain boundary. Determine compatible grain orientations and a common tilt axis, then choose suitable initial sizes and an available Ni potential to run the initial minimization. If possible, 
Analyze which sigma grain boundary  this configuration most closely resembles.
After minimization, analyze possible short and long structural periods without assuming a repeat ratio. Show useful diagnostic plots and compare candidate PBC x sizes and their mismatch. Save the results in project memory and leave the final size choice to me.

## FCC Ni (110) ∥ (111) tilt boundary

| Grain / plane | X | Y | Z |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top, GB1 (110) | [0 0 −1] | [1 1 0] | [1 −1 0] |
| Bottom, GB2 (111) | [1 1 −2] | [1 1 1] | [1 −1 0] |

**Misorientation:** 35.2644°; common **〈110〉 tilt axis** [1 −1 0]. Y is the GB normal; Z is the tilt line.

**Closest CSL reference:** **Σ9 at 38.9424°**, with **Δθ = 3.6781°** (bounded search: Σ ≤ 50, plane indices ≤ 5). Construction retains the original (110) ∥ (111) geometry.

### Candidate periodic X cells

| Candidate | Top : bottom | PBC X (nm) | Relaxed (%) | Build (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P006 | 5 : 2 | 1.7630 | 1.9960 | 2.0204 |
| P012 | 11 : 4.5 | 3.8830 | 0.2512 | 0.2060 |

**P012 is the review-priority candidate.** P006 exceeds the <2% build-mismatch limit; P012 passes, and its half-integer bottom coefficient is FCC-compatible. Relaxed mismatch uses the mean grain length; build mismatch uses the maximum. Final cell selection remains yours.

NiCr.adp, a₀ = 3.52 Å. The source relaxation did not formally converge (`linesearch alpha is zero`); longer modulation remains unresolved within the finite observation window.

## Load-drop analysis

All **71 finite points** were included; all loading steps converged. The analysis used the absolute top-boundary shear stress and a robust MAD threshold of **49.18 MPa**.

### Main result

The curve is dominated by one major load drop:

- Peak: **834.786 MPa** at step 36, \(\gamma=0.00900\)
- Next point: **2.511 MPa** at step 37, \(\gamma=0.00925\)
- Drop: **832.275 MPa** in one strain increment

This event is supported by both the robust-threshold and local-extrema detectors. All frames listed below are exact saved frames.

| Event | Peak step | Peak strain | Peak stress (MPa) | Valley step | Valley strain | Drop (MPa) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 36 | 0.00900 | 834.786 | 37 | 0.00925 | **832.275** |
| 2 | 39 | 0.00975 | 20.786 | 41 | 0.01025 | 20.470 |
| 3 | 43 | 0.01075 | 21.960 | 45 | 0.01125 | 20.076 |
| 4 | 47 | 0.01175 | 22.206 | 49 | 0.01225 | 18.124 |
| 5 | 51 | 0.01275 | 17.810 | 52 | 0.01300 | 11.602 |
| 6 | 54 | 0.01350 | 17.998 | 56 | 0.01400 | 13.961 |
| 7 | 58 | 0.01450 | 19.723 | 60 | 0.01500 | 17.873 |
| 8 | 62 | 0.01550 | 21.192 | 64 | 0.01600 | 20.846 |
| 9 | 66 | 0.01650 | 22.181 | 68 | 0.01700 | 19.634 |

The eight post-event oscillatory drops span **11.602–20.846 MPa**, with a median of **18.879 MPa**. The first drop is approximately **44 times** larger than that median. Only the first event exceeds the robust abrupt-drop threshold; the later events are local peak-to-valley extrema.

![Stress-drop diagnostic](artifacts/analysis/stress_strain/stress-strain-20260927-044120-a8c0ed/stress_strain_curve.png)

**Interpretation:** the curve clearly identifies a major mechanical relaxation between steps 36 and 37, followed by low-stress oscillations. The curve alone cannot establish whether this is GB sliding, dislocation activity, structural-unit rearrangement, or a periodic-seam effect. That requires comparing the saved atomic structures immediately before and after the event.

Analysis run: `stress-strain-20260927-044120-a8c0ed`  
[Reusable event data](artifacts/analysis/stress_strain/stress-strain-20260927-044120-a8c0ed/stress_strain_analysis.json)

In principle, the grain boundary sliding resistance should be a constant value; however, a massive stress drop occurred in our current loading mode, which is a phenomenon that theoretically should not happen. One possible reason is that the grain boundary structure underwent a permanent change during the first load drop. One verification method involves performing a reverse loading process in 70 equal steps to unload the strain back to zero and checking for differences between the two structures; the simplest approach is to examine the stress. If a difference exists, it indicates that the structures are distinct; one can then use NEB calculations to determine the minimum energy path and the configurations connecting the two structures.

Your proposed reverse-loading test has been completed.

## Reverse unloading result

Starting from the exact final state of the forward shear run, I applied **70 reverse \(-x\) increments of \(2.5\times10^{-4}\)**:

- Initial cumulative strain: \(+0.0175\)
- Final cumulative strain: \(-1.04\times10^{-17}\), effectively zero
- Final step: converged
- One intermediate reverse-path point did not converge and was retained in the curve

At nominal zero strain:

| State | Top shear stress |
|---|---:|
| Original forward-path reference | \(-0.000714\) MPa |
| Reverse-unloaded endpoint | \(+12.105451\) MPa |
| Residual difference | **\(+12.106165\) MPa** |

The reverse path remained on a low-stress branch, with maximum absolute stress **21.256 MPa** at cumulative strain \(0.0145\). It did not retrace the high-stress forward branch.

![Forward and reverse stress–strain paths](artifacts/analysis/stress_strain/stress-strain-20260927-045018-d12bcb/stress_strain_comparison.png)

## Interpretation

The residual stress and pronounced hysteresis provide evidence of **mechanical state retention** after the major load drop. This is consistent with—but does not by itself prove—a permanent GB structural transformation. Other possibilities, including incomplete endpoint relaxation or effects associated with the fractional periodic repeat, should still be checked.

Before launching NEB, the strongest next sequence would be:

1. Compare the original zero-strain structure with the reverse-unloaded zero-strain endpoint using atom-ID-matched displacements and GB plan views.
2. Confirm both candidate endpoints are locally minimized under identical box and boundary constraints.
3. If they remain distinct, use those consistently minimized structures as NEB endpoints.

No NEB calculation has been launched yet.

## Zero-strain displacement comparison

I compared the original minimized configuration against the reverse-unloaded endpoint using exact atom IDs.

- Atoms matched: **11,052 / 11,052**
- Unmatched atoms: **0**
- Reverse endpoint strain: \(-1.04\times10^{-17}\), effectively zero
- Estimated interface position: \(y=-0.7032\) Å

| Region | Atoms | Median displacement | Maximum displacement | Median XZ projection |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Entire structure | 11,052 | **0.2971 Å** | **0.7805 Å** | 0.2961 Å |
| Two facing GB layers | 174 | **0.3044 Å** | **0.7805 Å** | 0.3044 Å |

![Atom-ID-matched displacement comparison](artifacts/analysis/render/render-20260927-045354-eda0d9/plan_view.png)

The arrows show current minus reference displacement projected into the GB’s XZ plane. They are enlarged by a uniform factor of approximately **4.93** for visibility; the tabulated values are the physical displacements.

### Interpretation

The two configurations are measurably different, consistent with the residual zero-strain stress. However, the displacement is **not strongly localized at the GB**:

- GB-layer median: 0.3044 Å
- Whole-system median: 0.2971 Å

Their similarity indicates comparable displacement throughout the cell rather than an unambiguous localized GB rearrangement. The current vectors include rigid translation and affine deformation; neither was subtracted. Therefore, this raw comparison alone does **not yet prove a permanent GB structural transformation**. An aligned/non-affine comparison would be more decisive before selecting NEB endpoints.

- [Displacement and interface data](artifacts/analysis/render/render-20260927-045354-eda0d9/gb_plan_view.json)

Comparison run: `render-20260927-045354-eda0d9`

However, the issue is that we only performed loading and unloading without actively introducing rigid-body displacement; therefore, what you refer to as atomic rigid-body displacement should be considered part of the atomic structural changes. Thus, the simplest approach is to conduct an NEB calculation and examine the Minimum Energy Path (MEP) to determine the intermediate process.

I agree with that interpretation: because no separate rigid-body correction was imposed, the collective displacement is part of the pathway connecting the two mechanically retained states. I therefore used the two nominal-zero-strain configurations directly as NEB endpoints.

## NEB minimum-energy path

A shear-boundary-constrained **18-replica NEB** calculation completed successfully with exact atom-ID and cell compatibility.

| Quantity | Result |
|---|---:|
| Initial state | Original minimized P012 GB |
| Final state | Reverse-unloaded post-collapse state |
| Final-state energy relative to initial | **−0.016 eV** |
| Number of detected saddles | **1** |
| Saddle replica | **9 of 17** |
| Saddle reaction coordinate | **0.578044** |
| Saddle energy relative to initial | **+0.085 eV** |
| Forward activation barrier | **0.085 eV** |
| Reverse activation barrier | **0.101 eV** |

![NEB minimum-energy path](artifacts/analysis/neb/neb-analysis-20260927-050841-24df21/neb_mep.png)

The energy increases monotonically from the original state to replica 9 and then decreases toward the reverse-unloaded state. No additional interior minima or maxima were detected. The derivative changes from positive to negative around replica 9, supporting a single transition-state region.

### Interpretation

The NEB result supports two distinct nearby metastable configurations:

- The post-collapse state is energetically favored by approximately **0.016 eV** under the imposed shear-boundary constraints.
- They are connected by one resolved barrier of approximately **0.085 eV** in the forward direction.
- This provides energetic support for a persistent configuration change after the original load drop.

The MEP alone does not identify whether the transition is GB sliding, structural-unit rearrangement, defect motion, or a periodic-seam response. To identify the intermediate atomic process, the most informative structures are **replicas 8, 9, and 10**, compared against endpoints 0 and 17.

One limitation is important: the archived profile does not include per-replica residual forces or a separate saddle-force convergence measure. Thus, the reported barrier is the resolved 18-replica MEP barrier, but its numerical precision should not be interpreted more finely than the available profile supports.

## Candidate secondary-misfit vectors

Both axial layers were analyzed. All reported minimum vectors occur on **layer 0 (A)**. Here, G1 and G2 are two lattice-basis representations of the same directed physical displacement.

| Cell edge | Minimum length | Layer | Signed G1 / G2 representations |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| C1–C2 | \(0.1112253a_0=0.3915131\) Å | 0 | \(\frac19[001]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{22}[\bar1\bar12]_{\rm G2}\); opposite: \(\frac19[00\bar1]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{22}[11\bar2]_{\rm G2}\) |
| C2–C3 | **\(0.07864817a_0=0.2768415\) Å** | 0 | \(\frac1{22}[11\bar1]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{18}[110]_{\rm G2}\); opposite: \(\frac1{22}[\bar1\bar11]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{18}[\bar1\bar10]_{\rm G2}\) |
| C3–C4 | \(0.1112253a_0=0.3915131\) Å | 0 | \(\frac19[00\bar1]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{22}[11\bar2]_{\rm G2}\); opposite: \(\frac19[001]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{22}[\bar1\bar12]_{\rm G2}\) |
| C4–C1 | **\(0.07864817a_0=0.2768415\) Å** | 0 | \(\frac1{22}[\bar1\bar11]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{18}[\bar1\bar10]_{\rm G2}\); opposite: \(\frac1{22}[11\bar1]_{\rm G1}/\frac1{18}[110]_{\rm G2}\) |

Thus, the shortest nonzero candidate magnitude is **0.276842 Å**, occurring on the C2–C3 and C4–C1 edges, with opposite signed directions.

These are geometric candidates for secondary-misfit Burgers vectors—not confirmed dislocations or Burgers-circuit measurements. There were no truncation, incomplete-analysis, or no-mismatch flags.

Equality of energy alone does not prove atom-by-atom identity, but the displacement fields should be interpreted in that context.
